cards.title: P1 · Close the controller bugs and smooth the camera
cards.body:
Three small correctness bugs in files you own, all cheap, all worth closing before more code leans on them — plus two camera checkboxes pulled forward because they are free.

1. **The prefab is out of sync.** `Assets/TopDownController/Demo/Prefabs/TopDownAimController.prefab` serializes `faceCursor`, `turnImmediately`, `strictCursorAim`, `faceCursorWhileDoingAction`, `ignoreWhileCursorOverUI`, `aimPlaneHeightOffset`, `minAimDistance` — but **not** `blockAttackWhenCursorOverUI` and **not** `strafeMovementStates`, both added to the .cs afterwards (lines 32 and 43). They run on their C# initialisers today. Any inspector touch silently rewrites the file.
2. **Three RaycastAll passes per frame.** `UISceneGameplay.IsPointerOverUIObject()` (`UISceneGameplay.cs:670`) does a full `EventSystem.current.RaycastAll`. It runs **four** times a frame: `TopDownAimController.cs:79`, `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:48` (inside `base.UpdateInput`), `TopDownAimController.cs:177`, and `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:260` (inside the non-virtual `UpdatePointClickInput`). A subclass-local cache only fixes three of them — the fourth needs a field the base can read, or accept it.
3. **`CurrentAimPosition` will NRE.** Its fallback branch dereferences `EntityTransform` with no null guard, unlike `UpdateTopDownAim` which does guard. The first consumer that reads it before `Setup()` completes throws.
4. **The camera hard-snaps for no reason.** `Assets/TopDownController/Demo/Prefabs/TopDownGameplayCamera.prefab` has `smoothFollow: 0` with `followSmoothing: 10` sitting unused, and `smoothZoom: 0` with `zoomDeacceleration: 10` unused; `FollowCamera.UpdateCamera` lines 118-127 branch on `smoothFollow`. These two ticks were pulled forward from ctl-camera-lead-and-smoothing (P3) so a no-code quality lift is not gated behind the lead work — that card now owns the lead only. They are safe to author on the prefab: `DefaultGameplayCameraController.Update()` rewrites `target`, `targetOffset`, `fieldOfView`, near/far and `enableWallHitSpring` from the controller every frame, but it does **not** touch `smoothFollow`/`smoothZoom`.

Done looks like: open the prefab, confirm both fields appear with the values you want, no null-ref on a cold boot, and a camera that eases instead of snapping.

cards.title: P1 · Cursor-aim top-down controller
cards.body:
The controller that makes this a top-down action game already exists and works: `Assets/TopDownController/Scripts/TopDownAimController.cs` (226 lines), a subclass of `MultiplayerARPG.PlayerCharacterController` that overrides only `UpdateWASDInput()`, `UpdateInput()` and `ManagedUpdate()`. It is live — `Demo/Scenes/00Init.unity:796` points `defaultControllerPrefab` at `Assets/TopDownController/Demo/Prefabs/TopDownAimController.prefab`.

What it does: projects the cursor through `CacheGameplayCameraController.Camera` onto a `Plane` at the character's feet (a plane, not a physics ray, so aiming still works over pits), calls `SetLookRotation(rot, true)`, re-sends `KeyMovement` with `GameplayUtils.GetMovementStateByDirection` for 8-way strafe, and redirects the kit's pending auto-turn via the `protected` `_turnToTargetPosition`. It also mutes the `Attack` InputAction while the cursor is over UI.

**Load-bearing ordering:** the aim lands inside `UpdateWASDInput()` so it runs *before* the base's `UpdateWASDAttack()` and `UpdateTurnToTargetToDoAction()` in the same frame. Move it to `ManagedUpdate` and every attack fires one frame late. **Landmine:** `RedirectPendingActionToCursor` also fires for `TargetActionType.UseSkill`, overwriting the ground-snapped aim an area skill just set — turn direction only, but it looks wrong at long range.

cards.title: P1 · Type explicit ids and fix registration rules
cards.body:
`BaseGameData.Id` (Core/Scripts/GameData/BaseGameData.cs:31) returns `string.IsNullOrEmpty(id) ? name : id`, and `DataId = MakeDataId(Id)` (:153) is a pure string hash (:180). I confirmed all six project assets ship `id:` EMPTY — both swords, `Legs001_G`, `ArmorTypes/Legs`, `ArmorTypes/Cloak`, `MapInfos/Prototype_World_01`. Renaming any of them silently changes its runtime identity and orphans every saved inventory row. GUIDs survive a rename; DataIds do not.

`Assets/1. Data/GameDatabase_G.asset` is an **explicit-list** database (60 items, 7 armorTypes at :113-120, 10 weaponTypes at :121-131, 4 attributes, 4 damageElements — all but three pointing into the kit Demo tree). An asset not in it, not in `NewCharacterSetting.startItems` and not on a registered PlayerCharacter simply does not exist at runtime, with no warning.

Registration cascades: `AddGameData` (GameInstance_Data.cs:1026-1037) calls `Validate()` then `PrepareRelatesData()`; `ArmorItem.PrepareRelatesData` (ArmorItem.cs:29-33) calls `AddArmorTypes(ArmorType)` and `WeaponItem` (WeaponItem.cs:565-569) pulls in its WeaponType and DamageElement. Register the ITEM and the types follow for free.

**Landmine — that same cascade silently kills forks.** `GameDatabase.cs:115` runs `AddItems(items)` BEFORE `AddArmorTypes` (:117) and `AddWeaponTypes` (:118); `LoadReferredData` repeats the order at :146-149. The item re-registers the type its OWN GUID points at, and `AddGameData` writes only when the DataId key is absent, returning true with no log. Fork `OneHandSword` today and it is DISCARDED: both swords still reference the Demo original (guid `68fba38e…`, verified at DarkFortressSword001_G.asset:598 and SyntySword001_G.asset:598), so Demo claims the DataId at :115 and your fork loses at :118. You tune a file the game never loads and every symptom points at the tuning being wrong. **The rule: forking a WeaponType, ArmorType or DamageElement means repointing EVERY referencing item's GUID and swapping the Demo row out of GameDatabase_G in the SAME commit.** The Legs fork works today only because `Legs001_G.asset:603` already points at `1. Data/GameData/ArmorTypes/Legs.asset`. Attributes (:112) and DamageElements (:114) load before items, so those forks currently win on ordering alone — repoint them anyway rather than trusting a line number.

**This overturns a recorded decision.** CHANGELOG.md:25-32 says `TwoHandSword.asset` was edited in place rather than forked because "a fork would change the DataId and orphan the registered `TwoHandSword001` item" and because "the `Demo/` tree has no upstream repo". The first is wrong — DataId is a hash of `id ?? filename`, so a fork keeping the filename (or typing `TwoHandSword` into `id`) is DataId-identical. The second is true for the GitHub mirror path only; the Asset Store update path overwrites `Demo/` wholesale. Write the reversal into the CHANGELOG once you have proven the rule.

**Landmine:** `Legs001_G` is registered in BOTH `Assets/1. Data/GameDatabase_G.asset:70` and the stale kit `Demo/GameData/GameDatabase.asset:99`. Only the former is loaded, and the duplicate will confuse you at 1am. Note `GameDatabase_G.asset:99` is a different row entirely (SyntySword001_G) — always qualify the full path before deleting a line.

Done: six typed ids, a conventions README carrying the repointing rule, one database owning project items, and a CHANGELOG that agrees with the board.

Data/GameData/README.md`: `<Name>_G.asset` naming, `id:` always typed, folder mirrors the type name, every new asset registered in GameDatabase_G in the same commit, plus the silent-failure list (unregistered asset, duplicate DataId, empty id, missing equipSocket, null icon, null dropModel).

cards.title: P1 · Upper-body attack mask + mid-swing mask fix
cards.body:
**Shipped 2026-08-30.** Attacks play on the torso while the legs keep strafing: `Assets/1. Data/AvatarMasks/SyntyUpperBody.mask` is set as `avatarMaskWhileMoving` on the attack `ActionAnimation`s. Standing still is left unmasked on purpose, so the swing's own footwork still reads.

`Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/ActionLayerMaskUpdater.cs` closes a real kit hole: `AnimationPlayableBehaviour.PlayAction` resolves the action mask **once** at swing start (`avatarMaskWhileMoving` -> `actionState.avatarMask` -> `CharacterModel.actionAvatarMask` -> `EmptyMask`) and never revisits it. Start an attack standing still, then walk, and the legs stay welded to the attack clip while the character slides. The component re-evaluates the same condition each LateUpdate against `LayerMixer` / `ACTION_LAYER` / `EmptyMask` and writes only on a state change.

**Landmine:** it touches no kit file but reads `PlayableCharacterModel.Behaviour`, `LayerMixer`, `ACTION_LAYER` and `EmptyMask` as public API. A Core mirror update that renames or hides any of them breaks the *build*, not quietly — re-check this file after every kit update.

**Landmine:** the kit's own `TopMask.mask` cannot be reused — its humanoid flags are fine but its transform paths are the demo rig's (`Root_M/Hip_L/...`), which do not exist on the Synty hierarchy.

cards.title: P1 · Write SETUP.md so a fresh clone works
cards.body:
Your working copy is fine — the packs are on the Windows machine at `D:\1. Unity projekt\MMORPG Granny`, and the `.gitignore` entries were written while using them. This card is about the **next** machine: a Windows reinstall, a laptop, a collaborator, or a clone made in a hurry two years from now. The repo root holds only `CHANGELOG.md` — no README — and the recovery instructions exist nowhere except as prose scattered through 529 changelog lines.

Three things silently break a fresh clone. **(1)** `.gitignore:108-146` excludes nine vendor paths — `Assets/Synty/`, `Assets/Polygon*/`, `Assets/Interface*/`, `Assets/AnimationBaseLocomotion/`, `Assets/Action RPG SFX V2/`, `Assets/Hovl Studio/`, `Assets/Kevin Iglesias/`, `Assets/Melee Weapons Pack 1/` and `Assets/2. Art/Blink/` — roughly 1.9 GB of purchased, re-downloadable content. **(2)** `.gitattributes` routes `*.fbx *.png *.wav *.tga *.psd *.ogg *.exr` through Git LFS and **349 tracked files are pointers**; Unity never says "this is an LFS pointer", it says the texture is broken, so the symptom does not name its cause. **(3)** Import order matters — open the project before the packs land and Unity re-resolves references against nothing.

The good news, and the line that makes the doc worth writing: the GUIDs reconnect on their own. Unity packages carry their own `.meta` files, so re-importing a pack to the same path restores the same GUIDs. That is why `SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab`'s 39 unresolvable references, `UIItemsDialog.prefab`'s 14, `Prototype_World_01.unity`'s 5 and `Legs001_G.asset`'s 1 all come back without hand-reassignment — but only if the path is exact. BLINK must land at `Assets/2. Art/Blink/` or 600+ icon GUIDs need reassigning by hand.

**Landmine:** a clone shows `Assets/2. Art.meta` with no `2. Art` folder beside it. Decide once whether that is an orphan to delete or a folder to restore, and say which in the doc rather than leaving the next person to guess.

Ten minutes of typing against a lost afternoon on the next machine.

**Done:** `SETUP.md` at the repo root takes someone from `git clone` to a clean Play-mode session with no missing references and no guessing.

cards.body:

With cursor aiming there is no click-selected target, so a one-hand swing damages exactly **one arbitrary body** inside its 1.5 m / 90-degree arc while the two-hander already cleaves the whole arc — two weapons behaving differently for no authored reason. Set it to 0 on the fork before touching any VFX. **data-ids-and-registration-discipline (P1) owns creating that fork and repointing the two swords at it** — this card only flips the flag on it.

**(a) Sockets.** `effectContainers: []` at `SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab` line 74615. `GameEntityModel.InstantiateEffect` `continue`s past any effect whose `effectSocket` is missing from the dictionary — no log, no warning. `WhiteHitEffect` (socket `Body`) is already the project-wide `defaultDamageHitEffects` in `00Init.unity:842` and starts appearing the moment `Body` and `Floor` exist. Copy the arrangement from `Male_CC.prefab:1362` or use the `SetEffectContainersBySetters` context menu.

**(b) Contact-point VFX.** `damageInfo.impactEffects` is `{fileID: 0}` on both `OneHandSword.asset` and `TwoHandSword.asset`. `MeleeDamageInfo.PlayMeleeImpactEffect` computes a position along the hit direction — this is the only channel that fires at the actual contact point rather than on the victim's torso. Author `Assets/1. Data/GameData/Effects/ImpactEffects_Melee.asset` (tag-keyed, with a `defaultImpactEffect` fallback) pointing at a Hovl Studio slash/spark.

**(c) Impact SFX.** Each `ImpactEffect.effect` is a `GameEffect` carrying its own `randomSoundEffects` — that is the correct home for Action RPG SFX V2 flesh and metal hits, distinct from the anticipation swoosh. Optionally add a per-weapon transient on `DarkFortressSword001_G.launchClipSettings`, which fires inside `AttackRoutine`'s trigger loop.

**(d) The weapon prefab cannot receive a launch event at all.** `Assets/1. Data/Prefabs/Weapons/SM_Wep_Sword_01_G.prefab` is a bare variant: `m_AddedComponents: []`, no `BaseEquipmentEntity` anywhere on it. `BaseCharacterModel.PlayEquippedWeaponLaunch` (`BaseCharacterModel.cs:997`) only calls `PlayLaunch()` when `CacheRightHandEquipmentEntity != null`, and that cache is filled from a `BaseEquipmentEntity` found on the instantiated weapon model — so today the trigger-frame event never fires and a blade trail has nowhere to hang. Add the component as a variant override and put the trail on `weaponLaunchEffects`. While in there: `m_RemovedComponents: []`, so the two **inherited MeshColliders** ride a hand bone through every swing and must be removed as overrides, not by editing the file the changelog describes.

**Landmine:** `WeaponItem.LaunchClip` reads **only** `launchClipSettings` (`launchClip` and `launchClips` are dead) and does `Random.Range(0, Length - 1)` — max-exclusive, so with five clips the fifth never plays. Pad the list.

**Landmine — forking a type is not enough on its own.** Fork the WeaponType into `1. Data` with its `id` typed verbatim (or an Asset Store reimport reverts it), **and repoint every item that references it by GUID in the SAME commit**. `GameDatabase.cs:115-118` runs `AddItems` *before* `AddWeaponTypes`/`AddArmorTypes`, and `WeaponItem.PrepareRelatesData` re-registers the item's own referenced type — so while `DarkFortressSword001_G.asset:598` still points at the Demo GUID `68fba38efbfdced49a5d1e2ae95c0026`, the Demo original wins the DataId and your fork is dropped **silently**. cards.title: P3 · Give the dash a body and a cooldown
cards.body:
The dash moves you 10 m and looks like an ice-slide: no animation, no cooldown, no sound under the feet. This card gives it a body. **Scope note:** the ~200 ms attack buffer, `CancelAttack()` and the cancel-on-dash rule moved to feel-input-buffer-and-combo — that card is the sole owner now, and it calls into the dash this card builds.

**Dash body.** `dashStartState` / `dashLoopState` / `dashEndState` are all `clip: {fileID: 0}` on `Assets/1. Data/Prefabs/SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab` at **three sites: 76072, 76878, 77709** — verified, each site carries all three fields, so phase 3's "76072-76092" names only the first block. Fill all three or the dash animates in one movement mode and snaps in the others.

**Cooldown.** There is none anywhere: `CharacterControllerEntityMovement.AllowToDash()` only checks grounded and is not virtual, so it is not yours to patch. Gate it in `TopDownAimController` by muting the `Dash` InputAction the same way `blockAttackWhenCursorOverUI` already mutes Attack. Start at 3 s.

**Footsteps.** `CharacterFootstepSoundComponent` (`Core/Scripts/Gameplay/CharacterSystems/CharacterFootstepSoundComponent.cs`) is simply absent from `SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab`, and the survey calls it out twice as doing a surprising amount of work for melee weight. Fill `moveFootstepSettings.soundData.randomAudioClips` from Action RPG SFX V2 — that is the branch the top-down WASD path lands on (`ManagedUpdate` switches on `Entity.ExtraMovementState` and `default:` is `moveFootstepSettings`; walk/sprint/crouch/crawl/swim are separate settings you can leave empty). Leave `audioSource` unassigned if you like: `Start()` builds a 3D `_FootstepAudioSource` child itself. It plays only while a Forward/Backward/Left/Right movement flag is set and `IsGrounded`, on `stepDelay / Entity.MoveAnimationSpeedMultiplier`.

**Landmines:** the InputAction mute trick disables the action *globally* for the frame and resets its press state — keyboard and gamepad bindings go with it, and a held button dragged across the boundary can drop the hold. And the footstep component fails silently: `GetRandomedAudioClip()` returns null on an empty array and `PlayOneShot(null)` is a no-op, so an unfilled `randomAudioClips` looks exactly like the component not being there. Do not fill the `[HideInInspector]` legacy `soundData` field — it only exists to migrate old prefabs.

cards.title: P3 · Lead the camera toward the cursor
cards.body:
The camera shows you nothing you are aiming at. Verified on `Assets/TopDownController/Demo/Prefabs/TopDownGameplayCamera.prefab`: `targetOffset (0, 0.75, 0)` fixed, `smoothRotateX/Y: 0`, zoom 6..20. Every game in the reference set biases the view toward the aim point.

**Scope note:** the two free checkboxes that used to sit on this card — `smoothFollow` and `smoothZoom`, both 0 today with `followSmoothing 10` / `zoomDeacceleration 10` unused — were **pulled forward onto ctl-controller-hygiene at P1**. Do not tick them here; the two cards must not collide on the same prefab.

The lead is a subclass job: override `CameraTargetOffset` (verified `public virtual Vector3` at `BasePlayerCharacterController.cs:81`) and return `base + lead`, where lead is ~20% of cursor distance clamped to ~3 m and smoothed over ~0.15 s. `FollowCamera.UpdateCamera:153` applies targetOffset in **camera space**, so this is a true screen-space pan. The same channel is where an additive decaying shake belongs later.

**This card consumes no hit events.** It reads `AimWorldPosition` and nothing else. The `AddCameraShake` hook below is *provided by* this card for feel-hitstop-shake-knockback to call — that card already carries `depends --> feel-combat-feedback-bus` and `relates --> ctl-camera-lead-and-smoothing`, which is the whole of the real coupling.

**Landmines:** (a) `DefaultGameplayCameraController.Update()` rewrites `CameraControls.target`, `targetOffset`, `fieldOfView`, near/far and `enableWallHitSpring` from the controller *every frame* — authoring those on the prefab does nothing at runtime, go through `AssignedCamera*` or the `Override*` layer. `smoothFollow`/`smoothZoom` are NOT overwritten, which is why they are safe to tick on the prefab (see ctl-controller-hygiene). (b) Never write to `Camera.transform` — `FollowCamera.UpdateCamera` erases it the same frame. (c) `FollowCameraControls.Recoil()` is euler-only and lerps with `Time.fixedDeltaTime` inside LateUpdate, so its ramp is framerate-coupled — do not make it the primary channel. (d) `FollowCamera` declares `private void OnDestroy()`; declaring one in any subclass hides it and leaks a `_CameraTargetFollower` GameObject per camera.

cards.title: P3 · Build one CombatFeedback event bus
cards.body:
Hitstop, camera shake, knockback and hit-flash all need the same trigger: *a hit landed on this client, right now, on this target*. The kit already broadcasts it and **nothing under `Assets/Scripts/` subscribes to any of it**. Build the bus first or every feel item re-derives its own trigger and they drift apart.

Write `Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/CombatFeedback.cs`.

**Attacker side** — `Core/Scripts/Gameplay/CharacterSystems/CharacterActionsSystem/DefaultCharacterAttackComponent.cs` exposes `OnAttackStart` (line 36), `OnAttackTrigger(int)` (37) and `OnAttackEnd` (38) as settable `System.Action` properties.

**Victim side, every client** — `DamageableEntity.onNormalDamageHit` / `onCriticalDamageHit` / `onBlockedDamageHit` / `onDamageMissed` (lines 40-43) are parameterless `UnityEvent`s invoked inside the `[AllRpc] RpcAppendCombatText` (line 237). **Server only** — `DamageableEntity.onReceivedDamage` (line 46) carries position, instigator, amount and weapon; anything authoritative (knockback) hangs off this one, not the RPC.

**Coalesce per swing from day one.** A four-target cleave must produce one shake and one impact sound with magnitude scaled by target count, never four stacked. Build the coalescing window into the bus, not into each consumer.

**Landmine:** the attack component is added at runtime (`BaseCharacterEntity.cs:215` `GetOrAddComponent<ICharacterAttackComponent, DefaultCharacterAttackComponent>()`), so subscribe after Setup, not in Awake, or you bind to nothing.
checklist: Create Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/CombatFeedback.cs with a single OnHitLanded(target, amountType, targetCount) entry point
Subscribe to DefaultCharacterAttackComponent.OnAttackTrigger after Setup, never in Awake
Subscribe to DamageableEntity.onNormalDamageHit / onCriticalDamageHit for client-side feedback

cards.title: P3 · Add hitstop, camera shake and knockback
cards.body:
The 200 ms that turns a swing into a hit. None of it exists — a case-insensitive grep for `shake` across all of `Assets/UnityMultiplayerARPG` returns one unrelated WebSocket enum. All three consume the CombatFeedback bus.

**Hitstop.** `Time.timeScale` does literally nothing in this kit: `BaseCharacterEntity.EntityUpdate:281` uses `Time.unscaledDeltaTime`, the PlayableGraph is `DirectorUpdateMode.Manual` fed that same delta, `GenericUtils.FrameBasedDelay` counts unscaled, and `PlayActionAnimationRoutine` waits on `WaitForSecondsRealtime`. A timeScale hitstop freezes particles and physics while the swing keeps going. Subclass `PlayableCharacterModel` and scale the delta forwarded by `UpdateAnimation(float)` (`PlayableCharacterModel.cs:113`). Budget 50-70 ms normal, 90-110 crit, 150 kill; take the max on a cleave, never sum.

**Landmine:** `AnimationPlayableBehaviour.IsFreeze` looks like the switch and is not — `PlayMoveAnimation()` reassigns it every single frame from `CachedData.FreezeAnimation`.

**Shake.** Never write to `Camera.transform` — `FollowCamera.UpdateCamera` rewrites it every LateUpdate. Call `TopDownAimController.AddCameraShake(direction, magnitude)` — the hook **ctl-camera-lead-and-smoothing provides**, layered onto its `CameraTargetOffset` override. Do not write a second override here: 0.06-0.10 units for ~120 ms, 2x on crit, 3x with a longer tail on a kill. `FollowCameraControls.Recoil` is euler-only and lerps with `Time.fixedDeltaTime` inside LateUpdate, so its ramp is framerate-coupled — not the primary channel.

**Knockback.** `BaseGameEntity.ApplyForce` (`BaseGameEntity_MoveFunctions.cs:385`) is public and implemented on `NavMeshEntityMovement` too; copy the direction math from `SkillKnockback.ApplyKnockback`. 0.3-0.5 m over ~0.1 s — more than that fights the NavMesh. Apply it **server-side from `onReceivedDamage`**, never from the `[AllRpc]` client event, or host and client disagree about where the monster is standing.

cards.title: P3 · Buffer attack input, then cancel and combo
cards.body:
A click during a swing is discarded outright — `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:506` bails at `if (PlayingCharacterEntity.IsPlayingActionAnimation()) return;` before it even reads the button, with no queue anywhere. This is the largest responsiveness win available and it needs no kit patch. This card owns the buffer, the cancel rule and the combo; `ctl-buffer-and-dash-weight` owns only the dash's own body and cooldown.

**Buffer.** `UpdateWASDAttack` is not virtual, but `RequestAttack()` is public (`PlayerCharacterController.cs:428`) and handles hand alternation itself. Record Attack presses into a ~200 ms buffer inside `Assets/TopDownController/Scripts/TopDownAimController.cs` and call `RequestAttack()` on the first frame `IsPlayingActionAnimation()` goes false. Roughly thirty lines in a file you own.

**Cancel.** `AttackComponent.CancelAttack()` is `public virtual` at `DefaultCharacterAttackComponent.cs:456` and the controller never calls it. The rule that feels fair rather than exploitable: uncancellable until `OnAttackTrigger` fires, freely cancellable after. Wire cancel-on-dash first, then cancel-into-next-attack once the buffer is in.

**Combo.** `DefaultCharacterAttackComponent` walks `_lastAttackAnimationIndex` in sequence only when `doNotRandomAnimation` is true (line 113), resetting to 0 after `animationResetDelay` (2 s, line 45). The component is **never on the prefab** — `BaseCharacterEntity.cs:215` adds it at runtime via `GetOrAddComponent`, so a runtime instance takes the C# default of `false`. Pre-place it on `SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab` with the flag ticked, and restore 3 right-hand clips (currently reduced to one; `01_R`/`04_R`/`05_R` measured at 0.267 / 0.317 / 0.283).

**Landmine:** attack arrays do not fall back — `GetRightHandAttackAnimations` tests `!= null` and an empty array is not null, so any weapon type given an entry must carry at least one clip or its attacks resolve to a zero-length action.

cards.title: P5 · Feed the cursor into UseHotkey for skillshots
cards.body:
`CurrentAimPosition` has existed since the controller was written and **nothing consumes it**. Today every non-area skill reaches `UpdateQueuedSkill` with `aimPosition.type == None`, because `UICharacterHotkey.OnClickUse` (line 417-425) calls `Use(default)` whenever `HasCustomAimControls()` is false — and `BaseSkill.cs:511` returns false for everything except `BaseAreaSkill`. That drops the cast into the `FindNearestAliveEntity` branch: a cursor-aimed game casting at whoever happens to be closest.

The fix is one override. `UseHotkey` is verified `public override bool UseHotkey(HotkeyType, string, AimPosition)` at `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:1034`, so this is a subclass change with no kit patch: intercept, and when the incoming `aimPosition.type` is None, substitute `CurrentAimPosition` (already a ready `AimPosition.CreatePosition(AimWorldPosition)`).

Do not double-aim those; check `HasCustomAimControls()` before substituting. Also null-guard first — see ctl-controller-hygiene, `CurrentAimPosition` currently NREs before Setup completes.

cards.title: P5 · Add a screen-space player cast bar
cards.body:
The player's own cast bar exists only as a world-space sliver above their head on `Demo/Prefabs/Gameplay/RelatesObjects/OwningCharacter/CanvasOwningCharacterUI.prefab`. At a top-down camera that zooms 6..25 that is unreadable, and nothing on the main HUD shows cast progress at all.

The cause is a class split, not a missing assignment. `UIGenericLayout.prefab` uses `UICharacter`, and `Core/Scripts/UI/Character/UICharacter.cs` has **no cast fields whatsoever** — only gages, stats, attributes and damages. The cast fields (`uiSkillCastContainer`, `uiTextSkillCast`, `imageSkillCastGage`, `sliderSkillCastGage`) live on `UICharacterEntity`, which is instantiated per-entity in world space. `UIUpdateCurrentCharacter.cs` binds a `UICharacter` to the playing character; nothing equivalent exists for `UICharacterEntity`.

So this is a ~15-line binder under `Assets/Scripts/UI/`: read `PlayingCharacterEntity.CastingSkillCountDown` and `CastingSkillDuration` (`BaseCharacterEntity.cs:121-122`) each frame, drive a fill image and a label, and hide the container when the duration is 0. No kit patch, no forked prefab, no new UI framework.

Do the enemy half first — `uiSkillCastContainer` / `imageSkillCastGage` on `UITargetCharacterHp.prefab:657`, owned by `world-readable-enemy-hud`. It is zero-code and it tells you whether a cast bar reads at all at this camera distance before you write a binder for the player's.

**Landmine:** `CastingSkillCountDown` counts **down**, not up. Fill from `1 - (CountDown / Duration)` or your bar drains as the cast progresses, which reads as exactly the opposite of what is happening.

**Done:** you start a cast and a bar fills on the HUD where you are already looking, not forty pixels above a character in a zoomed-out scene.

cards.title: P5 · Rebind the action bar to M1/M2/QWER

`Demo/Prefabs/UI/_Gameplay/Standalone/UIHotkeys_Standalone.prefab` is ten `UICharacterHotkey` instances with `key: 48..57` (Alpha0..Alpha9) and `buttonName:` empty on all ten, plus ten `TextKey` children hardcoded to "1".."0". The plumbing is already there: `UICharacterHotkey` polls `InputManager.GetKeyDown(key) || InputManager.GetButtonDown(buttonName)`, and `GetButtonDown` resolves the name through `inputActionAsset.FindAction`, so a mouse-bound ability only needs a named action in `InputActions.inputactions`. Once M1 carries an ability the two fight. Both `UICharacterHotkeys.Update` and `UICharacterHotkey.OnClickUse` are non-virtual, so removing the confirm means swapping the script on your forked prefabs or patching the kit and logging it.

cards.title: P5 · Build a real death screen
cards.body:
The Escape defect is no longer this card — `ui-death-escape-guard` owns that one-line guard at P2, because phase 1's done-condition guarantees you meet it in the first session. What is left here is presentation, and all of it is missing.

`CanvasGameplay_G.prefab` lines 231-284: `onCharacterDead` calls `Show()` on the UISystemDialog instance and `SetActive(true)` on its `ButtonRespawn` child; `onCharacterRespawn` reverses both. There is no fade, no "You died", no timer and no death camera. Dying opens the pause menu.

Respawn itself already works — `UISceneGameplay.OnClickRespawn()` at `UISceneGameplay.cs:507` sends `RequestRespawnMessage{option:0}` — so nothing here is netcode. It is a panel and two event rewires.

**Landmine:** with `deadState.clip` still null, `AnimationPlayableBehaviour.SetBaseState` returns early, `CLIP_DEAD` is never registered and the corpse plays locomotion under your new overlay. Fill it first (`feel-hurt-and-dead-states`, all five sites) or the screen looks broken for the wrong reason.

**Landmine, and it is the good outcome:** a panel built outside UISystemDialog escapes `UIEscapeWindowsHandler`'s collected set entirely, which lets the P2 guard be retired rather than carried forever. Check that before adding a second exclusion on top of the first.

**Done:** you die, the screen dims with a readable message and a respawn button, and respawning drops you at the map's startPosition.

cards.title: P5 · Give the orc a telegraph worth dodging
cards.body:
The mechanism exists and is invisible. `OrcWarrior.asset` lists Bash at `useRate: 0.75`; `Demo/GameData/Resources/Skills/Bash.asset` has `castDuration: 0.5` and `coolDownDuration: 5`, chosen by `MonsterCharacter.RandomSkill` inside `MonsterActivityComponent.UpdateAttackEnemy`. But there is no wind-up pose, no ground marker and a 90-degree cone, so half a second of cast reads as nothing happening.
Monsters cannot charge — `DefaultCharacterChargeComponent.StartCharge` is reached only from `ShooterPlayerCharacterController.cs:2007` — so telegraph shape has to be built on the skill cast path: `SkillAnimations.castState` plus `skillActivateAnimation` on the model, `SkillCastEffects` (instantiated at `DefaultCharacterUseSkillComponent.cs:230`), and `AreaDamageEntity` for a ground marker. `BaseSkill.canBeInterruptedWhileCasting` decides whether hitting it mid-cast cancels the swing.
**Landmine:** `RedirectPendingActionToCursor` in TopDownAimController also fires for `TargetActionType.UseSkill` and overwrites the `_turnToTargetPosition` an area skill just set from its clamped ground-snapped aim point. Only the turn direction is affected, but it looks wrong on long-range casts — fix or scope it here.
**Done:** you can see the orc wind up, dash out of the marked area on purpose, and watch the hit land where you were standing.

Assign a Hovl ground decal or ring to the skill's skillCastEffects so the danger zone is on the floor, not just over the head

cards.title: P5 · Add hover soft-targeting and an [E] prompt
cards.body:
Nothing in the project knows what is under the cursor: `TopDownAimController.TryGetCursorWorldPosition` raycasts a mathematical `Plane`, never physics, and `UIBaseGameEntity`'s Visibility enum has no hover mode. There is also no desktop interaction prompt at all — `ActivateButtonActivator` is referenced by exactly one prefab (the mobile layout) and it only shows and hides, never naming the target or the key.
The hooks all exist. `FindClickObjects(out Vector3)` is public at `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:30` and wraps `_physicFunctions.RaycastPickObjects` with `GetTargetLayerMask()`; `_physicFunctions` is protected and `SelectedEntity` has a protected setter. Writing it lights up both the world nameplate and the `UITargetCharacterHp` frame for free, because `PlayerCharacterController.cs:280` already pushes `UISceneGameplay.SetTargetEntity(SelectedGameEntity)` every frame. `ShouldShowActivateButtons()` is virtual and walks `ActivatableEntityDetector.activatableEntities`, a `readonly List<IActivatableEntity>` on a detector created at `PlayerCharacterController.cs:210`.
**Landmine:** `PlayerCharacterController_Inputs.cs:549` sets `SelectedEntity = FindNearestAliveEntity(...)` on every swing. Hover has to coexist with that write frame to frame — decide explicitly whether hover or the swing wins while attacking, or the two will fight.
**Done:** hovering an orc shows its name and health without hitting it, and standing near an NPC or a ground drop shows "[E] Talk to <Title>".

Write the hover result into SelectedEntity and write down the precedence rule against the swing-time write at line 549

cards.title: P6 · Build a game-data validator window
cards.body:
There are at least seven ways to author a game-data asset that fails silently, and by phase 6 there will be dozens of assets rather than six. The project already has the right precedent for this kind of tooling — `Assets/Scripts/Editor/SceneShortcutsWindow.cs` and `SyntyEquipmentContainerBuilder.cs` show that a small EditorWindow fits how you work.

The checks worth automating, all confirmed in code: an asset under `1. Data/GameData` that is not in `GameDatabase_G` (explicit-list database, no warning ever); two assets whose Id hashes to the same DataId (`AddGameData`, GameInstance_Data.cs:1031, keeps the first and logs nothing); an empty `id:` (BaseGameData.cs:31 falls back to the filename); a `WeaponItem` with `moveSpeedRateWhileAttacking: 0`, which is the C# default and a full-swing movement freeze; a null `icon` or `dropModel`; an `equipSocket` string absent from SyntyPlayerCharacter's container list; and an `instantiatedObjectIndex` past the end of its container's groups.

The highest-value check is the fork-repoint one: any item in `1. Data` whose `weaponType` or `armorType` GUID still resolves into `Demo/`, while a same-DataId fork exists in `1. Data`. That is the failure `GameDatabase.cs:115-118` causes silently, and it is trivial to detect statically.

Build the checklist before the tool — the tool is only worth writing once the manual list has caught you out two or three times and you know which checks actually fire.

Done: one menu item that lists every offending asset with a click-to-select row, run before each commit that adds game data.
checklist: Write the manual checklist into `Assets/1. Data/GameData/README.md` first and use it for a few authoring sessions before writing any code.
Add `Assets/Scripts/Editor/GameDataValidatorWindow.cs` following the SceneShortcutsWindow pattern (menu item, scrollable list, click to select the asset).
Implement the registration check: every BaseGameData under `1. Data/GameData` must appear in GameDatabase_G or in NewCharacterSetting_G.startItems.
Implement the identity checks: empty `id`, and duplicate DataId across every registered asset.
Implement the fork-repoint check: flag any item whose `weaponType`/`armorType` GUID resolves into `Demo/` when a same-named fork exists under `1. Data/GameData`.
Implement the equipment checks: unknown `equipSocket`, out-of-range `instantiatedObjectIndex`, null icon, null dropModel, and `moveSpeedRateWhileAttacking == 0` on any WeaponItem.
Run it once across the whole project and fix everything it finds.

cards.title: P6 · Cut the project loose from the Demo tree
cards.body:
Every playable session boots `Assets/UnityMultiplayerARPG/Demo/Scenes/00Init.unity`, and the project's entire identity lives as three edits inside it: `gameDatabase` → GameDatabase_G (line 834), `uiSceneGameplayPrefab` → CanvasGameplay_G (line 790), `defaultControllerPrefab` → TopDownAimController.prefab (line 796). That tree is exactly what an Asset Store package update overwrites — so today, the fix for the February/August drift destroys the project's configuration.
The drift is **not** a compile risk (only 9 .cs files exist across all Demo trees, all in DevExt, all already fixed). It is silent field remapping, and it has already fired: `Warrior.asset` lost its whole `addressableIcon` block and had `ammoCapacity` split into `ammoCapacityModifier`/`ammoCapacityRate` purely from being saved. Treat any Feb-era demo prefab that behaves oddly as data loss, not a bug.
**What this card does not sever:** `CanvasGameplay_G.prefab` nests **18 Demo prefab instances** — `UIDialogs`, `UISystemDialog`, `UISettingDialog`, `UIGenericLayout` (the entire player HUD), `UIHotkeys_Standalone`, `UIChat`, `UIPartyAndQuest` — plus the 8 `CombatText` prefabs it points at, plus `OrcWarrior.prefab` until the orc fork lands. Creating `00Init_G.unity` re-points three references; it does not detach that tree. Believing otherwise means believing a reimport is safe when it would still overwrite the live HUD.
**Landmine:** `Demo/Scripts/DevExt/DevExtDemo_CharacterStats.cs` injects `public float testStat1` into the CharacterStats **struct** via a partial declaration, and it is now serialized into 112 assets including SyntyPlayerCharacter.prefab and all three gear items. Deleting DevExt is correct and produces a 112-file diff — do it in a commit of its own, never mid-feature.
**Done:** an Asset Store reimport of `Demo/` can no longer change which database, controller or canvas the game boots with — and whatever still lives inside `Demo/` is written down rather than assumed gone.

Make it scene 0 in ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset and trim the list from 17 scenes to it plus Prototype_World_01

Finish the fork-on-touch pass on the Demo ScriptableObjects you still depend on (remaining ArmorTypes, DamageElements, the four PlayerCharacters, StatusEffects) with ids preserved and Demo rows removed from GameDatabase_G

Delete the stray kit-tree files — Demo/Scenes/Map001_G.unity, Demo/Prefabs/UI/Item/1. Backups/, the two orphan Armors metas, Assets/2. Art.meta, the unreferenced Assets/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions — and remove the inert STEAMWORKS_NET define in the same pass

Enumerate what still lives in Demo/ afterwards — the 18 prefab instances nested inside CanvasGameplay_G, the 8 CombatText prefabs, OrcWarrior.prefab, UIHotkeys_Standalone — and record in Tools/KitPatches/README.md that a reimport still reverts any edit made inside them

cards.title: P6 · Play the loop with a friend over LAN
cards.body:
"Playable with a friend" has two answers and picking late is expensive. LAN needs zero code today: the NetworkManager in 00Init.unity is `LanRpgNetworkManager` (guid ee13c7c5...), networkAddress localhost / port 7770, already implementing `StartHost(withDiscovery)`, `StartClient` and a `LiteNetLibDiscovery` broadcast, with `UILanConnection` as the join UI and `DefaultGameSaveSystem` persisting the host's world to local files. Over Tailscale or ZeroTier the client just types the host's address.
The MMO module is complete and unmodified: `MMOServerInstance` reads `-startDatabaseServer` / `-startCentralServer` / `-startMapSpawnServer` / `-startMapServer`, and `SQLiteDatabase` self-creates 34 tables at `./mmorpgtemplate.sqlite3` with no external server. Half a day proves whether it boots, before there is content to migrate.
**Landmine:** `MMO/Demo/Prefabs/GameInstance.prefab` points at the stock CanvasGameplay (line 73), the stock PlayerCharacterController (line 78) and the kit GameDatabase (line 182). Under MMO netcode you silently get tab-target combat with none of this work unless those three are re-pointed.
**Landmine for the feel layer:** shake and hitstop are client-side by design, but knockback must be applied server-side off `onReceivedDamage`, never from the `[AllRpc]` client event, or host and client disagree about where the monster is standing.
**Done:** two people fight the same orc, both see damage numbers and drops, and nothing desyncs — and the LAN-vs-MMO decision is written down in the CHANGELOG.

cards.title: P6 · Build a Synty-rigged second enemy
cards.body:
Phase 6's done-condition is "the arena has shape", and today it is reachable with exactly one enemy type forever: `world-own-the-orc` forks the demo orc and nothing on the board builds a second archetype. This card is the only path to an enemy that is not a kit demo orc.

The cheapest first monster is a humanoid on the **same Synty FixedScale modular rig as `SyntyPlayerCharacter`**, because everything expensive about it is already proven: the avatar, the retargeting, `Assets/1. Data/AvatarMasks/SyntyUpperBody.mask`, the measured trigger rates (0.317 / 0.267 / 0.283 for the 1H clips, 0.350 for 2H) and `Assets/Scripts/Editor/SyntyEquipmentContainerBuilder.cs`. A bandit or a cultist costs a prefab and an appearance pass, not a new animation pipeline.

Copy the component list verbatim from `Demo/Prefabs/Gameplay/CharacterEntities/OrcWarrior.prefab`: `MonsterCharacterEntity`, `MonsterActivityComponent`, `NavMeshAgent` + `NavMeshEntityMovement`, `CharacterModelManager`, `PlayableCharacterModel`, `DefaultCharacterAttackComponent`, `CharacterRecoveryComponent`, `CharacterSkillAndBuffComponent` — plus the `_TpsCamTarget` / `_CombatText` / `_MeleeDamage` / characterUi / miniMapUi child transforms, which are as load-bearing as the components and are the ones people forget.

Re-run the container builder against the new model for armed and unarmed variety: the same tool that repairs the player's wardrobe (`data-repair-synty-wardrobe`) gives this monster its silhouette for free, and the variant index still reads the same as Synty's own mesh numbering.

**Landmine:** null model states do not fall back the way you expect. `SetBaseState` skips null clips so locomotion falls back, but attack arrays do **not** — `GetRightHandAttackAnimations` tests `!= null` and an empty array is not null, so an empty entry resolves to a zero-length action and the monster swings at nothing.

**Landmine:** register both the MonsterCharacter asset and the prefab in `GameDatabase_G` with an explicit `id:` typed in, in the same commit. An unregistered asset does not exist at runtime and logs nothing at all.

**Done:** two visibly different enemies fight you with different reach and timing, and neither one is a Demo prefab.

cards.title: P6 · Sculpt the arena into a real space
cards.body:
`Assets/New Terrain.asset` is 1.96 MB that gzips to 5.4 KB — 81.9% zero bytes: a dead-flat, untextured, propless 500x500 plane centred on the origin. Every fight in it is identical, the camera's 6..25 zoom range buys nothing, and the NavMesh bake is currently meaningless because there is nothing to path around, so obstacle avoidance and leash behaviour have never actually been tested.
It also sits at the Assets root, outside the `1. Data` convention, unnamed. `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset` preserves the GUID, so moving and renaming it keeps the scene reference intact — do that first, before more scenes reference it.
Top-down action combat reads through spatial contrast: a chokepoint to kite around, cover that breaks line of sight, elevation to frame the camera, a landmark so you know where you are.
**Landmine:** the NavMeshSurface bakes relative to its own transform inside the `3. Map` group, and `m_CollectObjects: 0` (All) means it bakes the whole scene regardless of its 10x10x10 size field. Sculpt, move or reparent anything and you must rebake, or `SpawnInternal` logs "cannot find grounded position" and re-queues forever.
**Done:** there is a chokepoint you can kite an orc around, cover that breaks line of sight, and at least one landmark you can navigate by.

Place two obstacles closer together than twice the 0.5 NavMeshAgent radius and confirm the orc routes around them rather than clipping through, then paint two terrain layers so slope and distance read at the top-down angle

Fight an orc around the new geometry and confirm it paths, leashes and never gets stuck

cards.title: P7 · Audit the official AimAtCursor addon
cards.body:
The kit creator pushed `UnityMultiplayerARPG_AimAtCursorController` on 2026-05-20, after `TopDownAimController.cs` was hand-written. It is not in this checkout (`Assets/TopDownController/` contains only `Demo/` and `Scripts/`, and a project-wide search for `*AimAtCursor*` returns nothing), so nobody has compared them. It may cover the same ground, cover it better, or — more likely — solve two or three edge cases the hand-built version has not hit yet.

This is deliberately parked, not forgotten. The hand-built controller works, its ordering is understood and documented, and replacing a working controller mid-combat-tuning would invalidate every timing measurement taken against it. Revisit after phase 5, when the aim surface has stopped changing.

What to look for specifically: how it handles gamepad (ours reads `InputManager.MousePosition()` unconditionally at `TryGetCursorWorldPosition`, so on a pad the character never turns); whether it uses a physics raycast or a mathematical plane (ours uses a plane on purpose, so aiming works over pits and gaps); whether it redirects `_turnToTargetPosition` the same way or patches `UpdateWASDAttack`; and whether it solves the area-skill turn conflict our `RedirectPendingActionToCursor` creates.

Done looks like: a short verdict written into CHANGELOG.md — adopt, cherry-pick named behaviours, or close the item permanently. Do not half-migrate.

Diff its aim projection, turn-to-target redirect and strafe handling against TopDownAimController.cs
Check whether it handles gamepad aiming and area-skill turn conflicts, our two known gaps
Write a one-paragraph verdict into CHANGELOG.md: adopt, cherry-pick specific behaviours, or close

cards.title: P7 · Park movement acceleration and gamepad aim
cards.body:
Two controller items are deferred on purpose. The reasoning is the park — without it written down, someone starts them.

**PARKED WITH PREJUDICE — movement acceleration and stop damping.** The survey rates it 'a few days, high impact'; I think it is a trap. Battlerite and Diablo both have near-instant acceleration, the weightlessness in this build comes from the missing dash, hitstop and footsteps that phase 3 fixes, and `CalculateCurrentMoveSpeed` is private inside a set of non-virtual functions behind `CharacterControllerEntityMovement` — so it is a kit patch you re-apply after every Core mirror update, forever. Evidence: `BuiltInEntityMovementFunctions3D.cs:1097` — `CalculateCurrentMoveSpeed` is `private` and contains only the `_lagMoveSpeedRate` lag-compensation ramp; line 942 is `tempMoveVelocity = tempHorizontalMoveDirection * CurrentMoveSpeed`, one frame from zero to full speed and back.

**REVISIT TRIGGER:** re-read this card after feel-hitstop-shake-knockback ships. If the character still reads floaty with dash, hitstop and footsteps in, unpark acceleration. That is the only condition — not a hunch, not a spare afternoon.

**Gamepad aiming.** `TopDownAimController` reads `InputManager.MousePosition()` unconditionally with no device branch, so a pad half-works today (movement, camera and six hotkey buttons are already bound in `Demo/InputActions.inputactions`). It is a day's work and changes nothing about how the game feels on the machine you develop on. Evidence: `TryGetCursorWorldPosition` line 216 has no device branch; `InputManager.MousePosition()` (`InputManager.cs:582`) returns `Mouse.current.position` or the primary touch, never a stick. `DefaultAreaSkillAimController`'s `_Mobile`/`_Console` branches are the template when you want it.

Revisit trigger for this one is external: the first time someone other than Sam plays with a pad.

cards.title: P7 · Park the minimap, harvestables and factions
cards.body:
Deliberately deferred — each with the reason written down **and** a trigger that says when to look again. A park without both is just forgetting.

**Minimap markers.** `Core/Scripts/UI/Minimap/UIMinimapRenderer.cs` ships a full marker system (playingCharacterMarker, ally/party/guild prefabs, MinimapMode, MapMarkerPrefabData) and a GUID search finds **zero** references to it anywhere in the project. notes.text:
HOW TO READ THIS BOARD

Title prefix and card colour are the phase: P1 blue, P2 copper, P3 bronze, P4 purple, P5 teal, P6 straw, P7 slate.

An arrow means "needs this first" — it points from the work at the dependent card to the thing it is waiting on. Follow the arrows backwards from anything you want, and you get its build order.

Labels are the subsystem: controller, feel, combat, enemies, gear, ui, data, world, netcode, tooling, risk.

Every card body names real files and real kit classes. The **Landmine** notes are the expensive part — they are the traps found by reading the Core source, not guesses.

START HERE — THE FIRST THREE

1. Put an orc in your own world. Add a MonsterSpawnArea to Prototype_World_01 pointing at OrcWarrior.prefab, bake it, and set startMap on Novice/Archer/Mage so any class lands there. OrcWarrior is ALREADY registered in GameDatabase_G with a hurt animation, a death animation, a 0.5s Bash telegraph and a 14-item drop list. It is standing in no scene. This is inspector work, not content work.

2. Set hitOnlySelectedTarget: 0 on OneHandSword and Unarmed. They are still 1; TwoHandSword is already 0. With cursor aiming there is no click-selected target, so a one-hand swing hits exactly one arbitrary body in its arc while the two-hander cleaves. One boolean.

3. Fork NewCharacterSetting so you start with YOUR gear. It is a plain ScriptableObject with no DataId and its startItems auto-register — hours, not days.

THE ONE PROJECT RULE

FORK ON TOUCH — never edit a Demo asset in place. Copy it into `1. Data`, keep the filename (or type the original name into `id`), and swap the Demo row out of GameDatabase_G in the SAME commit.

DataId is a plain hash of `id ?? filename`, so a fork keeping its name is DataId-identical. The CHANGELOG's TwoHandSword entry says otherwise and is wrong — see data-ids-and-registration-discipline.

THE CATCH: forking a WeaponType, ArmorType or DamageElement also means repointing every item that references it by GUID, in that same commit. GameDatabase.cs runs AddItems (:115) BEFORE AddArmorTypes (:117) and AddWeaponTypes (:118), and PrepareRelatesData re-registers the item's own referenced type — so the Demo original claims the DataId and your fork is dropped SILENTLY. No error, no log.

THE SEVEN PHASES

P1 · Boot the machine — You press Play as any class, land in Prototype_World_01, an orc walks across the screen and starts hitting you, a training dummy stands nearby, and every Demo-tree edit you have made is written down in one file.
P2 · Make contact legible — Every hit, in both directions, produces something you can see and hear at the moment the blade arrives rather than nothing at all — and you can watch an orc's health bar drain while it staggers.
P3 · Weight and responsiveness — A landed hit freezes, kicks the camera and pushes the target; a click during a swing is never dropped; the dash is a real move with a start, a slide and a recovery — and you have re-measured the trigger rates against all of it.
